scope: scripts/qualify_interruption.py, TIA V21 owned scratch projects, one artifact root per scenario. Each scenario terminated the exact worker and its owned TIA, or the exact Host, at a journal-observed boundary; a fresh Host and fresh owned TIA called engineering_admission_reconcile once; the change journal was unchanged by reconciliation and no mutation was re-dispatched. Results: change_apply killed while applying -> released (project unchanged vs retrieved checkpoint); killed while checkpointing -> held (no complete checkpoint archive); Host killed while applying (dispatchIntent, worker finished and saved) -> released (project verifiedApplied: fresh fingerprint equals the journal's afterFingerprint); change_restore killed while retrieving -> held (partial destination project cannot be opened; original project unchanged, archive unchanged); project_retrieve killed -> released (destination verifiedApplied); scratch creation killed -> held (partial project cannot be opened); library_create_master_copy apply killed -> held; library two-checkpoint restore killed at its first retrieval -> released (7 resources: originals not written, archives unchanged, destinations without content); the real held simulation_download admission 63974f72776f486ebbbd111464869c2f -> released (report completed after admission and card manifest matched; project LastModified 13:27:15Z UTC before admission 13:28:13Z).
limitations: Case restore-kill-preserving failed: the qualifier's plain 20 ms journal reads blocked the worker's File.Replace, so change_restore failed with EngineeringError before writing 'restoring' (journal.json.new left behind). Rerun after the fix in local.engineering.interruption.rerun.20261024.

The library_create_master_copy hold came from a matcher bug (a library checkpoint below its admitted directory was not matched, so write times decided); fixed and rerun in local.engineering.interruption.rerun.20261024.

Interruption is process termination of the worker and its owned TIA, or of the Host; power loss, disk faults and network transport to a remote worker are not exercised. Each scenario ran once; where the kill landed inside a phase is timing-dependent and recorded per case.
TIA reported Project.LastModified with DateTimeKind.Utc in every case.
